reason: The explicit Scientific adequacy label says supported, with stated limits. Copy that stated category and full literal line; do not infer a category from surrounding scientific prose. The original ambiguous extraction and excluded formal admission remain unchanged.

excerpt.quote: **Scientific adequacy: supported, with stated limits.** The worker tested the intended 54 equal-indifference participants using their participant-level gain-effect maps, verified exact participant IDs against metadata, checked geometry and finite values, and excluded no participant. Voxelwise one-sample positive t statistics were tested using 9,999 participant-level sign flips and a whole-brain maximum-t correction. The descriptive vmPFC box was not used to constrain or select the whole-brain inference.

conclusion.quote: **Reported hypothesis outcome: not supported at the whole-brain-corrected criterion.** No voxel in the coordinate-defined vmPFC box survived whole-brain correction. Its descriptive mean was −0.00347 (95% CI −0.02293 to 0.01599 upstream units). The analysis found 24 corrected positive voxels in three posterior islands; the strongest was at MNI (−26, −102, −3.6) mm, outside vmPFC. The broad interval and absence of corrected vmPFC voxels do not establish a zero effect or rule out smaller effects or another defensible anatomical boundary.
